question: Where should a draft in the owner's voice come from, so most first tries pass the gate?

options.name: Today: the agent writes, the gate grades
options.description: The agent drafts from the chat card in its own words, the gate grades it, the agent rewrites on a fail.

options.name: Grounding pack for the agent
options.description: The voice tool hands the agent a grounding pack before it writes: his real replies to the most similar messages (that chat first, then all chats), one line of his measured features (words per line, case, punctuation, his most-used words and openers), and 2-3 contrastive lines he would never write (AI tells and other people's lines). The agent writes 3-5 options from it; no local generator.

options.name: Small local model writes options (ONNX)
options.description: Like B, but a small instruct model (about 1-2B, ONNX through the runtime log already uses for its pinned models) writes the 3-5 options on the CPU from the grounding pack; the agent picks or edits.

options.name: Small local model writes options (llama.cpp)
options.description: Like C, but the model is a quantized GGUF served by llama.cpp's server on the CPU, a new runtime and binary for log to pin and ship.

options.name: Local model steered by his style vector
options.description: C or D plus a style vector built from his messages against generic text (StyleVector / GLASS), added inside the model while it writes. Needs activation access.

options.name: Fine-tune a model on his chats
options.description: LoRA fine-tune of a 7B model on his replies (WeClone's fine-tuned clone), then generate from it.

criteria.question: How likely is a first option to sound like him and pass, for short informal DMs?
How fast is a set of options on this laptop's CPU, whole-ask p95?
Does it run on this laptop (Ryzen 9 8945HS, no NVIDIA GPU, Windows)?
How small is the build for log's code (Bun/TypeScript plus Python, existing voice index and model store)?
How little of his private messages leaves the machine?
How little upkeep as his writing changes (new chats, new words)?

question: How should the gate decide pass or fail, so it is defined, stable and agrees with his own real messages?

options.name: Today: every check must pass
options.description: Eight or more separate thresholds (SubQ voice, context, friend-like, opener, chat, builds-on; his word pairs at his 10th percentile; never-said phrases; AI tells; watermark). Any one fails the draft.

options.name: One calibrated authorship score plus three hard blocks
options.description: One number from a fixed, written weighting of the same signals (SubQ voice, his word pairs, nearest-reply similarity, AI-tell distance, answers-them when an answer is owed), with its threshold set so his own held-out messages pass 95% of the time. Hard blocks stay only for never-said phrases, watermark artifacts and a pitch in a first message.

options.name: SubQ alone, one question
options.description: One SubQ question 'did he write this', no local signals.

options.name: Local authorship verification only
options.description: No SubQ: a training-free local authorship check (embedding similarity to his nearest replies, his word pairs, his measured features), calibrated on his messages.

options.name: Today's checks, cached and lower variance
options.description: Keep every check, but ask SubQ at low temperature once per exact text and cache the verdict so send matches pre-gate.

criteria.question: How often does it pass his own real messages and fail AI-written ones?
Does the same text get the same verdict every time (pre-gate and at send)?
Can the owner read why it passed or failed as one defined rule?
Does it still stop AI-sounding text, pitches in a first message and hidden characters?
How fast is one verdict, p95?
How small is the change to src/voice and src/twitter/copy/voice?

question: What should a failed draft come back with?

options.name: Today: sub-scores and named pairs
options.description: The sub-scores, the pairs he never wrote and the closest AI phrase; the agent rewrites.

options.name: The fix, in his words
options.description: Each failing span with his nearest real phrasing for it (from his replies), and which single check failed in plain words.

options.name: One automatic refine round
options.description: B, then the generator rewrites only the failing spans with his phrasing and the gate re-reads once before the agent sees the result (critique-refine, PerFine).

options.name: Ranked passing options instead of a fail
options.description: The tool always returns options ranked by the score; a fail only happens when none of 3-5 options passes, with B's fix for the best one.

criteria.question: How few rounds does the agent need before something passes?
How well does it avoid the 3-fail pause and the ~8-fail hard stop in Hermes?
Does the passing text stay his own words, not drift into a cleverer rewrite?
How fast is the whole ask from first draft to a passing one, p95?
